classification.difficultyReason: Model the labelled right triangle using Pythagoras, solve a non-monic quadratic and calculate an area for each valid root.

content.prompt: The lengths of the sides of a right-angled triangle are $(3x+1)$ cm, $5x$ cm and $(5x-2)$ cm. Find the area of the triangle.

spec.sourceRegion: Review exercise question 10, triangle below the stem
spec.description: A is lower left, C lower right and B directly above C. Ordinary source-blue edges are rendered black under house style. No shading.
spec.mathematics: AB=5x, BC=3x+1, AC=5x-2; angle ACB is a right angle. Side lengths are in centimetres.
spec.answerVisibility: All labels and the right-angle marker are permanent givens; no answers are shown.

answer.short:
$6\text{ cm}^2$ or $\dfrac{28}{27}\text{ cm}^2$.

Use Pythagoras to find both valid values of $x$, then calculate half the product of the perpendicular sides.
answer.worked:
Since $AB$ is the hypotenuse, Pythagoras gives

$$\begin{align*}(3x+1)^2+(5x-2)^2&=(5x)^2\\9x^2+6x+1+25x^2-20x+4&=25x^2\\9x^2-14x+5&=0\\9x^2-9x-5x+5&=0\\9x(x-1)-5(x-1)&=0\\(9x-5)(x-1)&=0\\9x-5&=0\quad\text{or}\quad x-1=0\\x&=\frac59\quad\text{or}\quad x=1\end{align*}$$

Both values give positive side lengths.

For $x=1$, the perpendicular sides are $3(1)+1=4$ cm and $5(1)-2=3$ cm:

$$\begin{align*}A&=\frac12\times4\times3\\A&=6\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$

For $x=\frac59$, the perpendicular sides are $3\left(\frac59\right)+1=\frac83$ cm and $5\left(\frac59\right)-2=\frac79$ cm:

$$\begin{align*}A&=\frac12\times\frac83\times\frac79\\A&=\frac{28}{27}\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
